title: For every positive n and nonzero complex moment parameter, a polynomial-loop morphism into projective tame symplectic quiver automorphisms maps any pair of rank-two Gibbons-Hermsen points with a regular semisimple X or Y
author: Igor Mencattini; Alberto Tacchella
work: A Note on the Automorphism Group of the Bielawski-Pidstrygach Quiver
source_version: Official SIGMA 9 (2013) article 037, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2013.037; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs compatible polynomial triangular and affine actions on a noncommutative doubled-quiver path algebra, passes them through an amalgamated product and its scalar quotient, and integrates necklace Hamiltonians explicitly. It then identifies the generators needed to move regular semisimple rank-two moment-map points into the Calogero-Moser submanifold, rather than obtaining the mapping property from an unrestricted transitivity assertion.

source_check.note: Full original Theorem 1, including both the polynomial-loop group morphism and its pair-mapping assertion, is retained with the rank-two quiver/moment setup, projective scalar quotient, necklace maps, Nagao amalgamation and complete explicit Hamiltonian differential equations, integrated flows and morphism proof. The assumptions are positive n and nonzero complex moment parameter; the regular semisimple condition is on X or Y. The original Remark 1 is retained: the subgroup does not preserve the regular locus, so no invariant-locus transitivity or injectivity is asserted. Prior Bielawski-Pidstrygach results and Calogero-Moser transitivity remain cited standard prerequisites. Routine displayed-generator conjugation calculations remain the source author checks; no Hamiltonian helper or higher-rank extension is separately counted. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: Full Theorem1, including the group morphism and the pair-mapping assertion, is selected. Read all of Section3, including Theorem4 explicit Hamiltonian differential equations and integrated flows, and the full morphism construction/proof on pages10-11. The quiver, moment parameter tau!=0, quotient by scalar affine automorphisms Z, necklace maps and Nagao amalgamation are on pages1-7. Prior published Bielawski-Pidstrygach Proposition7.2 and Lemma8.4 and Calogero-Moser transitivity are cited background; no new unexpanded local proposition is substituted for the author core. The subgroup P does NOT preserve R_n,2, as Remark1 explicitly states; the selected conclusion maps each pair of points, and makes no invariant-locus transitivity or injectivity claim. Routine generator/conjugation calculations following the displayed maps are authored ancillary checks; no additional counted Hamiltonian lemma or higher-rank generalization.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1 over C, n>=1, r=2, tau!=0: Gamma_alg=Gamma_alg_sc x PGL_2(C[z]), Gamma_alg_sc={exp(p) I_2:p in z C[z]}, admits the displayed morphism into PTAut(A;c)=TAut(A;c)/Z for the doubled Bielawski-Pidstrygach quiver. P is generated by its image and the exact formal Fourier automorphism F of (14). For every pair xi1,xi2 in R_n,2, where either X or Y has distinct eigenvalues and is diagonalizable, an element of P sends xi1 to xi2. R_n,2 need not be P-invariant; neither injectivity nor all-point transitivity is claimed.
